# Maximum Cusp Height

Maximum stair-step deviation on sloped surfaces.

<figure markdown="span">
![Maximum Cusp Height: on the left what to avoid, on the right what to aim for](../../assets/diagrams/max-cusp-height-light.svg#only-light){ width="640" }
![Maximum Cusp Height: on the left what to avoid, on the right what to aim for](../../assets/diagrams/max-cusp-height-dark.svg#only-dark){ width="640" }
<figcaption>Stair-step deviation on shallow slopes, measured normal to the surface.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Where it applies

| Process | Criticality |
| :-- | :-- |
| [FDM](../../reference/processes/fdm-3d-printing.md) | Low |

## Values

**Aim for** is what to design for; crossing it gives a warning. **At most** is the hard limit; crossing it gives an error. See [aim for and limits](../../concepts/aim-for-and-limits.md).

Criticality in this process: **Low** ([what this means](../../concepts/criticality.md)).

| Material | Aim for | At most | Source |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Default** | 0.10 mm | 0.15 mm | Not yet sourced |

Every other material uses the Default values: PLA, PLA-CF (Carbon Fiber), PETG, ABS, ASA, TPU (Flexible), PA, PA-CF (Carbon Fiber), PC.

## Messages

What the results panel says about a finding. You can rewrite these in the Process Library; the words in `{braces}` are filled in for each finding.

!!! warning "Warning"

    Cusp height `{measured}` exceeds the recommended `{target}`. At this surface angle each printed layer creates a visible step. Expect a rough surface finish on this face.
!!! failure "Error"

    Cusp height `{measured}` exceeds the `{limit}` limit. Layer steps are clearly visible and the surface will feel rough to the touch. Steepen the surface, reduce the layer height, or plan to sand after printing.
| Placeholder | Replaced with |
| :-- | :-- |
| `{measured}` | The measured value, with its unit |
| `{target}` | The rule's "Aim for" value |
| `{limit}` | The rule's "At most" value |
